rules.name: War of Japanese Aggression
rules.description:
China was a divided country without strong political ties to western allies. Ammunition and weapon shortages combined with untrained conscripts and brutal conditions made victory extremely difficult. China was almost always on the defensive.

Before any game, a Chinese battlegroup can always choose to be the Defender in an Attack/Defense scenario rather than be the Attacker or play a Meeting Engagement scenario. The choice is up to the Chinese player. This rule overrides the Horu rule for the Japanese.

profiles.name: Dare to Die Platoon Command Squad

rules.name: Dire Consequences
rules.description: This battlegroup is fighting a major battle that must not be lost. The dire state of the war means that the troops are desperate to avoid devastating consequences at the hands of the Japanese. At the start of the game, roll 2 D6 and add the result to the battlegroup’s total BR.

rules.name: International Spectacle
rules.description: Intense fighting at large international cities has drawn the attention of the world. Newsreels from bystanders are recording this battle. Any sign of weakness might dissuade desperately needed potential allies. At the start of the game, roll a D6 and add the result to the Battlegroup’s total BR.
